proposed.explanation:
EFID's FY2025 consolidated results show strong and accelerating growth: revenue rose ~29.5% to EGP 20.92 bn, gross profit rose ~44.2% to EGP 7.19 bn, and net profit surged ~67.7% to EGP 2.70 bn. Earnings per share doubled from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. At the current price of 20.40 EGP, the trailing P/E is roughly 9.4×, which is modest for a company growing earnings at this pace, suggesting the market has not fully priced in the improvement.

This fits the investor's profile well: a 5–7-year horizon allows time to ride out volatility, the high willingness to accept losses is appropriate for a single-stock position, and no planned withdrawals mean the shares can be held through any drawdown. The medium financial ability to withstand losses is the main caution, so I am sizing the position at 1,200 shares (EGP 24,480), which is about 49% of the 50,000 EGP portfolio—just under the 50% single-company cap—leaving EGP 5,520 in cash as a small buffer.

Risks and uncertainties: (1) Only two years of data are available; a single year of strong growth does not guarantee a sustained trend. (2) No balance-sheet, cash-flow, or sector-competitive data are provided, so leverage, working-capital needs, and industry cyclicality cannot be assessed. (3) The stock is a single holding, so company-specific risk is concentrated. (4) The P/E calculation uses the most recent reported EPS; if growth slows, the multiple could expand or contract. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
